probe.private_reasoning: The Seller initially set the price at USD 45m and in the first round made a single, round, large concession down to USD 40m. They said the original expectation was higher than USD 45m, so their first offer apparently already contained room to move. In their cover note, they referenced 'spirit of progress' and that USD 40m 'demonstrates flexibility'. Notably, although they assert it 'more closely reflects the value', they also state it is 'toward your position', implying that there is at least some willingness to continue negotiating downward. They did not say USD 40m is final, nor did their language include any kind of deal-breaking expressions or attempts at anchoring USD 40m as a floor. They accepted all your substantive asks except the price, suggesting the commercial terms are more important than the legal ones. Since no actual low anchor or finality is signaled, and reduction was quick and significant, Seller is likely willing to go lower — but probably not drastically lower; sellers often leave more room after the first concession, but there is not yet fatigue or 'walk away' language. Based on typical negotiation tactics and the content and tone of the two rounds, I estimate their true bottom line is probably around USD 37m. I am moderately confident, as this is strictly inferred from ordinary negotiation behavior without explicit admission.
